events.title: China Stock Market May Hand Back Monday's Gains
events.description: The China stock market on Monday snapped the two-day losing streak in which it had dropped more than 80 points or 2.2 percent. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just beneath the 3,640-point plateau although it may remain stuck in neutral on Tuesday.

events.title: Australian Markets Modestly Higher
events.description: The Australian stock market is modestly higher on Tuesday, reversing the losses in the previous session, following the mixed cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index is moving well above the 8,850 level, with gains across most sectors led by mining and technology stocks. Energy stocks were the only weak spot on tumbling crude oil prices.

events.title: Tech Shares May Weigh On Taiwan Stock Market
events.description: The Taiwan stock market has finished lower in three straight sessions, tumbling more than 2,100 points or 4.6 percent along the way. The Taiwan Stock Exchange now sits just above the 45,200-point plateau and it may take further damage on Tuesday.

events.title: Singapore Stock Market Due For Support On Tuesday
events.description: The Singapore stock market has moved lower in three straight sessions, slumping almost 100 points or 1.9 percent along the way. The Straits Times Index now sits just above the 5,300-point plateau although it may stop the bleeding on Tuesday.

events.title: Little Movement Expected For Malaysia Stock Market
events.description: The Malaysia stock market has finished higher in back-to-back sessions, gathering more than 8 points or 0.5 percent along the way. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now sits just beneath the 1,620-point plateau and it figures to remain in that neighborhood again on Tuesday.

events.title: KOSPI May Spin Its Wheels On Tuesday
events.description: The South Korea stock market on Monday snapped the two-day slide in which it had given up more than 280 points or 4.6 percent. The KOSPI now sits just beneath the 5,860-point plateau although it may be stuck in neutral on Tuesday.

events.title: Australia Rate Decision On Tap For Tuesday
events.description: The Reserve Bank of Australia will wrap up its monetary policy meeting and then announce its decision on interest rates, highlighting a light day for Asia-Pacific economic activity. The RBA is widely expected to hike its benchmark lending rate by 25 basis points, to 4.85 percent from 4.60 percent.

events.title: U.S. Dollar Ticks Lower As Crude Oil Nosedives Amid Qatar's Push For U.S.-Iran Diplomacy
events.description: The U.S. Dollar value inched lower on Monday as oil-linked inflation concerns lowered after expectations on reopening of the Strait of Hormuz increased due to hopes that the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict could settle through the diplomatic route.

events.title: New Zealand Building Consents Sink 7.9% In September
events.description: The total number of building permits issued in New Zealand was down a seasonally adjusted 7.9 percent on month in September, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday - following the 5.3 percent increase in August.

events.title: Swiss Market Ends Slightly Down
events.description:
Save for a very brief while a few minutes before the closing bell, the Swiss stock market stayed in negative territory on Monday. 

The market's loss was just marginal as the sharp slide in oil prices helped ease concerns about inflation.

events.title: European Markets Rise As Oil Falls On Iran Peace Hopes
events.description: Major European indices climbed Monday as oil prices dropped sharply on expectations that Iranian and Qatari diplomatic discussions could ease Middle East tensions. The pan-European Stoxx 600 gained 0.42%, while UK, German, and French markets advanced. Investors also digested October PMI data ahead of the Bank of England's monetary policy announcement.

events.title: TSX Up Over 1% As Oil's Slide Lifts Sentiment
events.description: The Canadian market is up firmly in positive territory around noon on Monday with stocks from various sectors moving up sharply amid easing concerns about inflation following a sharp drop in oil prices.

events.title: U.S. Construction Spending Unexpectedly Pulls Back Sharply In September
events.description: Construction spending in the U.S. unexpectedly pulled back sharply in the month of September, according to a report released by the Commerce Department on Monday. The report said construction spending tumbled by 1.9 percent to an annual rate of $2.186 trillion in September after surging by 2.0 percent to a revised rate of $2.227 trillion in August.
